gaps.sentence: 'Don't be late again,' the coach told him. The coach told him ___ late again.
gaps.explanation: Negative commands: not to be, with the negative before the whole infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'I'd love to come,' she said. She said she ___ love to come.
gaps.explanation: 'I'd love' is I would love; would does not change in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'I've lost my keys,' she admitted. She admitted that she ___ her keys.
gaps.explanation: Present perfect backshifts to past perfect: have lost → had lost.

gaps.sentence: 'You broke my phone!' she said to her brother. She ___ her brother of breaking her phone.
'The shop closes at six,' she reminded me. She reminded me that the shop ___ at six.
gaps.explanation: Even habitual present simple backshifts after a past reporting verb: closes → closed.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll call you later,' he promised. He promised that he ___ call me later.
gaps.explanation: Will backshifts to would in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'We won't stay long,' they said. They said they ___ stay long.
gaps.explanation: will not → would not (wouldn't) after a past reporting verb.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll carry those bags for you,' he said. He ___ to carry my bags.
gaps.explanation: Offers of help are reported as offered to do something.
